correctness.rationale: The four-dimensional three-ball cross-section integration and rational-trigonometric identity are explicit and symbolically cross-checked; both apparent u=±s poles are removed before classifying boundary roots. For 0<s<π, the numerator equals the strict tangent-line deficit of cos(sqrt(t)); convexity on [0,π²] and the lower bound cos≥−1 beyond prove uniform all-u positivity. The first boundary roots occur at ±3π. Compactness forces nearest-zero subsequences to these points, and analytic implicit-function minimization proves the exact -36π²/α² correction. Finite tests are corroborative, not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: This calculates the exact previously variational threshold ρ_4 of first Fourier zeros for the canonical high-dimensional counterexample family, proves its sharp boundary zeros, and determines the first nonlinear nearest-zero correction. The natural invariant is the nearest real Fourier-zero distance in an explicit isoperimetric problem; the sharp strip is substantially stronger than previously sufficient Bessel positivity radii and yields a useful exact finite-dimensional ball-comparison bound. The claim is structural rather than a routine numerical cutoff.
